objective: Mean TripAdvisor Rating per (AttractionType, Continent) for Indonesia, annotated with destination macro indicators.

data_sources.dims: User.xlsx (33,530 users, ContenentId), Item.xlsx (30 attractions, AttractionTypeId), Type.xlsx (17 types), Continent.xlsx (6 rows incl. id 0 '-')
macro: countries of the world.csv -> GDP ($ per capita)

steps: Loaded 5 sheets with pure-python xlsx_reader.read_xlsx (no openpyxl) and cast Ids/Rating to int.
Built fact view: Transaction -UserId-> User(ContenentId) -AttractionId-> Item(AttractionTypeId) -> Type; inner joins, 52,930 in / 52,930 out (0% row loss).
Aggregated mean(Rating) grouped by (AttractionType, Continent), rounded to 4 decimals; group sizes kept internally for reliability checks. Zero-review combos left absent (not zero-filled).
Looked up destination country = Indonesia in both macro tables (Country string .strip() for whitespace) and broadcast the two scalars (left-join on a constant key).
Sorted by AttractionType then Continent; wrote output.csv (UTF-8, no index) with exactly the 5 required columns.

validation_checks.check: weighted mean (w = reviews per group) reconciles with raw mean
8 groups with n<5 flagged low-confidence (not filtered)

interpretation_notes: Visa_Free_Score = 74 (Henley rank 66) describes the OUTBOUND mobility of the Indonesian passport, not Indonesia's inbound visa openness; it is context for the origin-market mix, not a driver of individual ratings.

GDP per capita 3,200 USD (World-Bank ~2006 snapshot) is constant across rows by construction; with a single destination it cannot explain cross-group variance — it only positions Indonesia as a mid/lower-middle-income destination, which is consistent with Beaches/Nature being the volume drivers (10,917 and 13,251 reviews) while high-end/high-touch products are thin.

Attraction type dominates continent: type means span 3.54 (Historic Sites) to 4.65 (Water Parks) ≈ 1.11 points, whereas continent means span only 4.088 (Africa) to 4.212 (Australia & Oceania) ≈ 0.12 points.

Polarising types (largest cross-continent spread): Speciality Museums 1.20, Ballets 1.07, National Parks 1.06, History Museums 0.78 — mostly small-n, so partly sampling noise. Universally liked / low-variance types: Water Parks 0.15, Points of Interest 0.17, Waterfalls 0.18, Volcanos 0.22.

Australia & Oceania rates highest overall (4.2124) and Asia supplies the most reviews (15,693); Africa has only 920 reviews, so its low mean (4.0880) and its 6 absent type combos should be read as thin evidence, not as a genuine continental judgement.
Beaches (3.85) and Historic Sites (3.54) are the weakest types despite heavy volume — the clearest actionable signal for the destination's product quality, independent of macro conditions.
